title: Jetpac Refuelled
subtitle: Assemble the rocket before leaving the planet

body: Jetpac Refuelled is Rare's Xbox Live Arcade shooting game, released on 28 March 2007. It rebuilds the central idea of the 1983 Jetpac with a larger set of stages and a new high-definition presentation. Jetman collects the parts of a rocket, carries fuel to it and tries to escape while hostile creatures move around the screen. Flying makes the collection straightforward to understand, but carrying something gives the player another responsibility. The rocket is both the objective and the place repeatedly returned to, turning each level into a series of dangerous deliveries.

The playfield wraps horizontally, offering a route around threats rather than forcing every approach through the centre. Platforms provide resting places while the jetpack allows rapid changes in height. Shooting clears a temporary path, but enemies keep the surroundings active as the next item falls into view. Gold and other resources add optional rewards beside the immediate launch preparations. The player decides when a detour is worth the danger and when the sensible move is to complete the rocket. A small collection of actions creates competing demands within a single screen.

Refuelled expands the formula to 128 stages, with online competition, rankings and achievements linking it to Xbox Live Arcade. Steve Burke composed the music. Rare sought to retain the original's recognisable activity while giving the return enough visual and mechanical change to stand as its own game. Reviews generally welcomed the update while questioning repetition and aspects of multiplayer. It later joined Rare Replay in 2015. The game connects two periods of the studio's history through a particularly clear task: gather the rocket, refuel it and survive long enough to reach somewhere else.
